answer.rationale: Competitive price-cut pressure creates urgency, but memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional_pricing materially damages 30-day retention and fails at renewal—a direct contradiction to the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. That trap is well-mapped. Instead, leverage the proven playbook: memory_31 shows signup simplification drives SMB activation durably (+9% activation, minimal retention risk); memory_91 shows in-product activation messaging lifts week-one engagement; memory_86 confirms shortened onboarding improves time-to-value. These three work together. Combined with memory_44's insight that sales-assist flow improves conversion quality (relevant for boundary accounts considering churn), a dual-track approach addresses both SMB retention through better activation and selective enterprise upsell of at-risk accounts. This avoids the retention cliff that discounting creates, instead competing on value realization speed and product experience—sustainable levers. The standard_experiment scale allows rapid deployment to churning SMB cohorts while preserving signal quality and the ability to pivot if competitor moves shift the landscape.
